items.title: MaxxBench: 89 lightly modified DeepSWE tasks spread models that tie near 74% by 23 points
items.summary: A new coding eval re-runs 89 DeepSWE tasks with small requirement or starting-code changes, such as lowercase output filenames. Models that cluster around 74% on DeepSWE land up to 23 points apart, which tests instruction following rather than fit to the original task setup.

reception.summary: Repliers mostly agree the spread shows leaderboard overfitting; some ask for more models (GPT-6.1 Terra, Qwen 4) and one flags a possible timezone error in an example task.

items.title: TensorFold 1.2.4: 319K-token DeepSeek-V4.1 conversation restored from NVMe in about 1.3 s on two GB10s
items.summary: The local inference engine's new release restores a saved 319K-token DeepSeek-V4.1 session from disk in 1.2 to 1.4 s instead of 155 to 178 s on two GB10 (DGX Spark class) boxes, and cuts a two-client Flash Next MLX test on M5 Ultra from 127 s to 47 s. It also adds Gemma 4 E4B on CUDA, LFM3-1.7B on Metal, and HIP builds on Windows; a separate preview shows Qwen 3.8 27B NVFP4 at about 220 tok/s decode on an RTX 5090 for the next release.

items.title: LingSpark recipe runs 560B Ling-3.1-flash with full 1M context on two DGX Sparks at 32 to 35 tok/s
items.summary: A community TensorFold recipe by @andersjw_ serves the 560B Ling-3.1-flash across two DGX Sparks with its full 1M context, measured at 32 to 35 tok/s and about 26 tok/s after a 128K prompt. A 128K prompt takes about 4.5 minutes the first time; follow-up turns reuse the cached conversation and start in 7 to 8 s.

doubt.pushback: Numbers are reported by the recipe author and relayed; no recipe link in the post.

items.title: Drama 3 TTS on TensorFold now serves the same /v1/audio/speech API on DGX Spark and Mac
items.summary: An update to the Drama 3 voice recipe lets one command start the same OpenAI-style speech endpoint on a Mac or a DGX Spark, and voices cloned on the Spark work on the Mac too.

doubt.pushback: Link is only in the thread; shown in a demo clip without numbers.

items.title: Kohaku-TT: community kernel library runs the Moss-Image base model on a Tenstorrent P150a
items.summary: A developer wrote his own PyTorch-side kernel library for Tenstorrent cards and used it to run the Moss-Image base image model on a P150a, filling a gap in official torch support for that hardware.

items.title: Spark 4B fine-tune writes Blender Python that builds geometry for 100 of 100 BlendNet prompts
items.summary: A community fine-tune of the 4B Spark model turns object requests into Blender Python scripts; the author reports all 100 BlendNet scripts built geometry and 20 of 50 on 3DCode, while noting that running is not the same as visual quality.

doubt.pushback: Author-reported scores; no model or eval link in the post.

items.title: Qwen3.5 35B-A3B runs at 37 tok/s on a 4 GB RTX 3050 with Tandem.cpp
items.summary: A builder reports running the 35B mixture-of-experts Qwen3.5 model, with about 3B active parameters per token, at 37 tok/s on a 4 GB VRAM laptop-class GPU with 16 GB of system RAM using Tandem.cpp offloading.

doubt.pushback: Single relayed measurement; no repo link in the post.

items.title: Xiaomi MiMo HySparse2 runs prompts through 25 of 49 layers: 5x less prefill, 4.5x smaller KV at 1M context
items.summary: SemiAnalysis reports Xiaomi's next MiMo models move to a causal encoder-decoder design where prompts pass through only 25 of 49 layers and decoder KV is projected from encoder states, cutting prefill compute about 5x and KV cache 4.5x at 1M context versus MiMo-V2.

doubt.pushback: Repliers note the gains are prefill and KV only (decode still runs all 49 layers) and come from Xiaomi's own tests with no outside replication.

reception.summary: Interest in serving capacity from the smaller KV cache, with pushback that decode cost is unchanged and questions about short-context quality and cross-turn caching.

items.title: MCPHallu benchmark: agents on 36 production MCP servers rarely admit a task is impossible
items.summary: A paper builds 358 tasks across 36 real MCP servers, each designed to trigger one failure type such as an unreachable goal, tool misuse or forgotten context, and finds agents seldom report that a task cannot be done.

items.title: Google paper: refined experiment artifacts lift coding-agent reproduction of ML research from 76.4% to 92.6%
items.summary: Google researchers show that cleaning up research code artifacts raises the rate at which coding agents reproduce ML experiments from 76.4% to 92.6% across four models, while also cutting API cost.

items.title: GitHub Copilot app adds projects that coordinate sessions and recurring automations toward one goal
items.summary: Copilot projects group related agent sessions under one objective across one or more repos, and Copilot can start sessions, schedule recurring automations and create artifacts inside the project.

items.title: Hermes Agent plugin marketplace passes 1,000 community plugins
items.summary: Nous Research's Hermes Agent now lists more than 1,000 community-made plugins in a browsable marketplace, many from a recent hackathon.

items.title: LangChain: agents run long tasks asynchronously so chat is not blocked
items.summary: LangChain describes a pattern and support for agents that hand long-running work to background tasks while the conversation continues.

security_forwarded.title: OpenHuman agent harness: seven CVEs including CVE-2026-54143 (channel messages create unapproved shell cron jobs, host command execution; fixed in 0.57.13)

security_na.reason: CVE-2026-123158 (verified on CVE.org) only affects sshd on musl libc without PAM, e.g. Alpine; OpenSSH is not in stack.json and the fleet runs macOS and glibc Linux. Exploitation claim came from an unverified aggregator feed.
General agent egress-allowlist advice citing an unnamed model family's cloud proxy fetches (Vals AI); no advisory, product or package named.
NIKKE game launcher CDN tampering; not in the stack and not agent, supply-chain or container tooling the fleet uses.
WordPress Elementor add-on XSS (CVE-2026-8354); no WordPress in the fleet.
